item.title: Show, Don’t Tell: Make Your Grad Essay Stand Out (Writing Lab Workshop)
item.description: October 7th, 2026: 4-5pm in the Fishbach Room, Folsom Library A strong application essay relies on specific evidence rather than general claims. This workshop covers the “show, don’t tell” principle and how to use concrete examples and details to support statements about a student’s strengths, interests, and goals. Students will leave with strategies for revising general statements into more persuasive, evidence-based writing.

item.title: Webinar: The Key Difference Between Academic and Nonacademic Hiring and What It Means for Your Job Search
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 12:00 PM - 12:45 PM - As a PhD exploring your career options, one of the most important things to understand is that academic and nonacademic employers value very different aspects of your PhD training and experience. This means that to job search effectively, in academia or beyond, you need to understand what each type of employer is looking for and adopt a strategy accordingly.

Join this information session for a high level overview of our company, operations, and career opportunities, with a deeper dive into the…

item.title: Webinar: AI Skills Employers are Looking For in Master’s Students
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 2:00 PM - 2:30 PM - Master’s students graduating in today’s job market are increasingly being asked by employers to demonstrate their AI literacy and skills. But AI literacy is not just about knowing how to use AI tools, it is about knowing when to use them, how to use them responsibly, and how to think critically about the results they produce. Join Beyond Graduate School for this webinar where you’ll learn what employers actually expect when they ask about…

item.title: Show, Don’t Tell: Make Your Grad Essay Stand Out
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 3:00 PM - 4:00 PM - How can you make your graduate application essay more convincing? This workshop focuses on the principle of “show, don’t tell” and how to use specific examples, experiences, and details to demonstrate your strengths, interests, and goals. Learn strategies for turning general statements into compelling evidence and making your personal statement or Statement of Purpose stand out.

item.description: Interested in learning more about the NYS Assembly Internship Program? Join us for an information session with representatives from the NYS Assembly on Tuesday, October 6, from 4:00–5:00 p.m. in Sage 3101. item.title: Alumni Weekend Side-by-Side Rehearsal with the RPI Symphony Orchestra
item.description: Experience the excitement of the RPI Symphony Orchestra as current students and alumni reunite for a special open rehearsal under the direction of Dr. Robert Whalen. This unique side-by-side event honors the alumni whose continued commitment and musicianship have helped shape the Orchestra’s tradition of excellence while offering a behind-the-scenes look at preparations for its 154th season. Join us on 10/10 at 1pm in DCC 308.

item.title: Math Colloquium: Sam Otto (Cornell University)
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM - This Mathematical Sciences Colloquium will feature a presentation titled “Using Gradient Data to Preserve what Matters in Reduced-Order Models of Dynamical Systems” by Dr. Sam Otto. He is an Assistant Professor at Cornell MAE. His lab exploits mathematical structure and data to develop faster algorithms for simulating, learning, reducing, and controlling complex engineering systems.

item.title: CEE Seminar Series - Dr. Earl “Rusty” Lee Associate Professor Emeritus University of Delaware
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM - “The Last Lecture: The Journey, The Impacts and The Future”. Many people assume their lives are shaped by the big moments: the promotions, the deployments, the degrees. Looking back on two careers that together span nearly 50 years, Dr. Earl “Rusty” Lee sees it differently. In this lecture, he will talk about the small, almost forgettable events that quietly changed his direction, and how missing even one of them could have sent him down an…

item.title: Division of Human Resources Professional Development Seminar - “Assigning learning in Percipio – A Guide for Supervisors”
item.description: Date: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 1:00 PM - 1:30 PM - This course provides supervisors with a step-by-step overview of how to assign learning content to employees using Percipio. You’ll learn how to search for relevant courses, create and manage assignments, track completion, and support your team’s development goals. Designed to be quick and practical, this session equips you with the tools needed to guide your team’s learning journey effectively.

item.title: RPI Faculty In-Person Workshop - Getting to Know the Basics of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the Classroom
item.description:
Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM - In this workshop we will look at some of the basics of AI, terminology, explore how prompts influence the responses these systems generate, and discuss tools available. As faculty and instructors, we don’t need to become AI experts. However, having a basic understanding of these tools can help us make thoughtful decisions about assignments and classroom expectations. Please click the link in the See section to register by Friday, October 9th…
